questions.prompt: Cross-platform application development refers to the ability to:
options: Develop an application once and run it on multiple operating systems or devices with minimal modification
Compile separate codebases per operating system
Run applications only inside the Java Virtual Machine
Convert desktop apps into mobile apps automatically
questions.explain: The slides' definition verbatim: **develop once, run on multiple OS/devices with minimal modification**.

questions.prompt: In the Java approach, source code is compiled into ______ which runs on the ______.
questions.explain: Java: source → compiler → **bytecode** → **JVM** → OS. "Write Once, Run Anywhere".

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts MPA and SPA?
options: MPA reloads the entire page per action; SPA loads once and updates sections via JS, with the backend returning JSON
MPA updates parts of the page; SPA reloads the entire page
MPA is client-centric; SPA is server-centric
MPA requires WebSockets; SPA requires CGI
questions.explain: MPA = server-centric full reloads; **SPA = one load, JS updates sections, backend provides JSON via API**.

questions.prompt: In a hybrid mobile app, the SPA runs inside a ______, and wrappers like Cordova/Capacitor/Ionic provide ______.
options: WebView container / a web-to-native bridge, plugin management and cross-platform packaging
questions.explain: Hybrid = SPA (HTML/CSS/JS) loaded by a **WebView** inside a native container. Wrapper roles: **web-to-native bridge, WebView container, plugin management, packaging** — they complement (not replace) Android Studio/Xcode.

questions.prompt: Which browser → rendering engine pairing is correct?
questions.explain: **Gecko = Firefox.** Chrome/Edge = Blink; Safari = WebKit; Trident = old IE.

questions.prompt: In an accessible HTML table, `scope="col"` on a `<th>` means:
options: The header applies to all cells below it in that column
The header applies to all cells to its right
questions.explain: `scope="col"` governs the cells **below**; `scope="row"` governs cells to the **right**.

questions.prompt: Which CSS line makes padding and border count INSIDE an element's declared width?
questions.explain: `box-sizing: border-box` makes padding+border part of the declared width — the lab's reset, predictable boxes.

options: Cards of at least 260px that fill the row and wrap automatically, with empty tracks collapsing
A single column at all widths
questions.explain: **auto-fit + minmax = responsive card grid**; empty tracks collapse so cards stretch. The lab's signature line.

questions.prompt: In the Quick Notes lab, why must `addEventListener` calls NOT be placed inside `renderNotes()`?
options: renderNotes() runs every time the list changes, so duplicate listeners would accumulate
Event listeners are forbidden inside functions
The browser only allows one listener per page
renderNotes() runs before the DOM exists
questions.explain: renderNotes() re-runs per change; listeners attached there would **stack up** — attach once in init() (or use event delegation on the parent).

questions.prompt: Which CSS pseudo-class selector is the home of custom properties (design tokens)? (type the selector)
questions.explain: `:root` = the document root — where custom properties live (`--color-primary: …`), read later with `var(--color-primary)`. No hard-coded hex allowed in the lab.
